gen-dafont-neuropol-gf-cascadia-code: Neuropol's slim opening in the c gives it a digital, outlined look. Cascadia Code follows in a wire-thin sans with generous gaps, and a larger heading size would let the difference in height show.
gen-dafont-neuropol-gf-julius-sans-one: Sharp, futuristic, and a bit closed off up top. Julius Sans One does the opposite job, with wide spacing and open-ended curves that let a sans-serif body breathe where Neuropol makes a statement.
gen-dafont-neuropol-gf-lexend-exa: A slim channel cut into the c marks Neuropol as digital and futuristic. Neuropol excels at announcing things in a display line, while Lexend Exa handles the steady work beneath it with wide curves and a big x-height.
gen-dafont-neuropol-gf-lexend-giga: Lexend Giga spreads its flat, single-weight linework across generously tracked words, with ascenders barely rising past the x-height. Against Neuropol's closed forms, that openness is the whole point.
gen-dafont-neuropol-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega looks drawn with one nib. Neuropol earns its keep when big and short, where its slim c opening and outline feel can stand out against that approachable body.
gen-dafont-neuropol-gf-lexend-peta: Futuristic from the first letter, Neuropol has a single-weight outline feel and a slim channel in its c. Make that heading small and it loses its edge, and Lexend Peta's wide-mouthed curves and big x-height would take over the page.
gen-dafont-neuropol-gf-lexend-tera: Digital edges up top, wide-open curves below. Lexend Tera reads like a plotter pen at work, its letters spaced like stepping stones, so a longer passage moves slowly and gets plenty of room.
gen-dafont-neuropol-gf-lexend-zetta: Lexend Zetta reads tall and widely tracked, its ribbon-like strokes staying constant in width. And if Neuropol were made small, its closed, outlined letters would lose the presence that a display heading needs.
gen-dafont-neuropol-gf-montserrat-altern: Montserrat Alternates brings a c as open as a bent paperclip, with round letters whose rims match the stems and lowercase crowding the capital line. Against Neuropol's closed forms, that openness is the strongest thing here.
gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-cascadia-code: Cascadia Code reads like fine wire, with wide gaps between neighbors and smooth curves all the way round. Oldtimer's round, parenthesis-like forms and flat downstrokes make the strongest contrast, classic and commanding above a modern plain sans.
